topic: Actaeon myth: Artemis turned him into a stag and his own hunting dogs killed him
title: His Own Dogs Killed Him After He Saw a Goddess Bathing
description: AI-narrated commentary on the ancient Greek myth of Actaeon, transformed into a stag by the goddess Artemis after stumbling on her bathing, then killed by his own fifty hunting hounds. Based on the account in Ovid's Metamorphoses.

hook_candidates.text: A hunter's own dogs tore him apart after he saw a goddess bathing by accident.
Would your dog still recognize you if a goddess turned you into a deer?
People assume a loyal dog could never turn on its owner. This ancient myth says otherwise.
Actaeon stumbled on Artemis bathing in the woods, and his own hounds made him pay for it.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists their dog would recognize them no matter what they looked like, because they want to prove even loyalty has limits.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a hunter's own dogs would always recognize him, no matter what he looked like.
closing_comment: Ovid actually turned Actaeon's own hunting dogs into named characters, all fifty of them, in his original poem.

sources.note: Confirms Actaeon was turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own fifty hounds.
Corroborates the myth: Actaeon saw the goddess bathing, was transformed, then killed by his own hounds.
